label: Toggenburg

names.text: 'Toggenberg' is the given aka and the spelling the Ceva page uses. 'Toggenburger' is the title of a Wikipedia article on the breed, seen in WebSearch result text only (that article was not opened). 'Toggenburg' is the item's label.

about.text: The Toggenburg is a brown, striped Swiss dairy goat named after the Toggenburg region of eastern Switzerland. It is one of the most productive dairy goat breeds and is distributed in about fifty countries across five continents.

sources.text: From the fetched Wikipedia article: named after the Toggenburg region, 'among the most productive breeds of dairy goat', and 'distributed in about fifty countries in all five inhabited continents'. The 'brown, striped' description is from the article's see-also summary in the Wikipedia Alpine disambiguation page, which was fetched; the Toggenburg article itself was not checked for that wording, so it is the least certain part of this sentence. The Ceva page calls it the oldest known dairy goat breed.

origin.place: Toggenburg region, Canton of St. Gallen, eastern Switzerland

sources.text: Wikipedia: named after the Toggenburg region of the Canton of St. Gallen, where it is 'thought to have originated'. Ceva lists Switzerland as the origin. The herd-book's start in 1890 is not a formation date for the breed, so no 'formed' range is recorded.

Both sources give 740 kg per lactation. The Wikipedia article gives it as the breed standard's minimum yield; Ceva gives 'around 740 kg of milk per lactation'. The figure is a minimum standard, not a recorded average, so min and max both hold it. No year or country is given, so none is recorded.
Ceva: 'with 3.5% fat and 2.9% protein', given with its 740 kg per lactation figure. The Wikipedia article's 3.56% fat and 2.90% protein are breed-standard minimums, so they are not used.
Both pages describe it as a dairy goat: Wikipedia calls it 'among the most productive breeds of dairy goat' and Ceva calls it 'the oldest known dairy goat breed'.

The fetched article says 'Worldwide, it is listed as not at risk' and that in Switzerland it is 'at risk/vulnerable'. The worldwide status is recorded here. The DAD-IS 2024 year comes from WebSearch result text citing Wikipedia's Toggenburger article (not opened), so the year is the least certain part of this field.

facts.v: The oldest known dairy goat breed.

sources.text: Ceva: 'Toggenburg is the oldest known dairy goat breed.'

facts.v: An estimated 3,235 to 7,273 in Switzerland in 2023, with just over 3,000 breeding females and 196 active males in the herd-book.

sources.text: From the fetched article: the 2023 Swiss population 'in the range 3235–7273', with 'just over 3,000 breeding females and 196 active males in the herd-book'.

facts.v: The first imports to the United States arrived in 1904.

sources.text: From the fetched article: 'The first US imports arrived in 1904.'
